Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the product walkthrough earlier today — it was very helpful. Per our internal sizing session, I wanted to capture Ava Systems' expected usage and the high-level budget parameters so you can put together a dedicated capacity proposal. Key details: 

- Expected daily token volume (generation + embeddings + chat history trim): ~20M tokens/day (~600M tokens/month)
- Average request pattern: mix of short chat responses and longer completions; median response ~80 tokens, 95th ~400 tokens
- Concurrency / throughput: peak concurrency ~40-60 simultaneous requests. We want sustained throughput to handle peaks with <300ms added latency beyond model generation.
- Model profile: evaluating a 65-70B family model (we'll provide exact model later). We'll be running quantized variants; important that KV cache and prefix caching are supported.
- Budget range: looking at $15k- $30k / month for inference costs (inclusive of reserved capacity amortized + support). This implies a target unit economics in the ballpark of $20- $50 per 1M tokens.

Ask: can you propose 1) a recommended reserved capacity configuration (GPU type + number of GPUs) to meet the throughput targets, and 2) a ballpark $/1M tokens calculation and monthly price range so we can evaluate against internal procurement? Also please include expected lead time for Dedicated (reservation + onboarding).

Would be great to have a short summary by Tue next week.

Thanks,
Rahul
Head of AI Infrastructure
Ava Systems

Marissa — did a quick back-of-envelope based on Rahul's baseline. Notes and assumptions below.

Assumptions:
- Model family: 65-70B (dense), quantized to q4_0 or q4_K; KV cache for chat workloads active
- Throughput measured in tokens/sec of generation (sustained): H100 (80GB) ~ 1,200-1,500 tok/s; A100 (80GB) ~ 850-1,100 tok/s (depends on perf tuning & compilation).
- Average response token count 80 -> average request generation time at 1,200 tok/s ~ 67ms generation; add network + request overhead = ~150-250ms depending on batching and qps.
- Peak concurrency target: 60 concurrent requests with 95th perc response sizes up to 400 tokens. We size for 95th to avoid throttling.

Sizing recommendation (to meet SLA & peaks with buffer):
- Option A (performance): 4x H100 (80GB) reserved. Provides headroom for bursts, autoscaling to 5-6 during sustained higher traffic.
- Option B (cost-balanced): 6x A100 (80GB) reserved. More GPUs but lower per-GPU throughput; closer to same aggregate throughput at slightly longer latencies.

Rationale: with 4x H100 we can sustain ~4,800-6,000 tok/s aggregate (using 1,200-1,500 tok/s per card), which supports peak scenarios and gives room for caching efficiency. With 6x A100 we'd be at ~5,100-6,600 tok/s aggregate at the higher end of A100 perf estimates.

Ballpark pricing math (very rough, for proposal):
- Cost to Redwood (infra + support + overhead) estimate per-month: H100 node (per-card) amortized = $8k- $12k; A100 node (per-card) amortized = $5.5k- $8k.
- Option A (4x H100) -> list price to customer (incl. platform + support) ~$38k- $52k / month.
- Option B (6x A100) -> list price ~$36k- $48k / month.
- Unit economics (simple $/1M tokens) given 600M tokens/mo: Option A -> $63- $87 per 1M tokens; Option B -> $60- $80 per 1M tokens.

Notes on lowering unit cost: smaller/quantized models, more aggressive batching, and prefix/KV caching can materially reduce consumed GPU cycles and lower $/1M tokens - we should run their typical prompt mix through our capacity sizer to refine.

Action items for pricing doc: Vanessa -> produce two neat option cards that reflect the numbers above and include a 12-month reserved discount scenario (we can offer 10-20% discount on committed annual spend). Also include lead time: ~4-6 weeks for Dedicated provisioning + onboarding.

--
Marcus
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
